targets.problem: Modern physical and differentiable vocal-tract simulators cannot determine the yielding-wall (soft-tissue) impedance of the vocal tract, because in air every loss mechanism — wall vibration, viscous/thermal boundary-layer loss, radiation, glottal leakage — scales together, so formant bandwidths in air do not identify them separately. Fleischer et al. therefore ran an 'extensive parameter study' and reported admissible wall values spanning three orders of magnitude. The hyperbaric diver-speech literature (c. 1968–1990) measured formant frequencies AND bandwidths for human speakers in helium-oxygen at 6–51 ATA, i.e. with gas density perturbed by roughly a factor of 8 and sound speed by 2.7 while the wall tissue is unchanged. That depth series is exactly the medium perturbation that breaks the degeneracy, and it appears never to have been used for wall-impedance identification. COMB TASK: recover the depth-resolved formant-bandwidth tables from the diving corpus and refit (m/A, b/A).
targets.notes:
B-TERMS / OLD VOCABULARY. Search 'helium speech', 'heliox speech', 'diver speech', 'divers' speech intelligibility', 'helium speech unscrambler', 'unscrambling', 'hyperbaric speech transcoder', 'formant shift relation', 'Fant–Lindqvist relation', 'wall vibration effect', 'soft-wall correction', 'yielding walls', 'cavity wall impedance'. Old papers report depth in msw/fsw/ATA/bar, damping as Q rather than bandwidth, bandwidths in c/s (cycles per second), and impedance in cgs acoustic ohms; modern papers use Hz and a damped spring-mass normalised as m/A in g/m^2 and b/A in Ns/m^3. That unit split is a real conversion hazard and is part of why the two literatures do not meet — convert carefully and state the conversion.

WHERE TO DIG. KTH STL-QPSR (Speech Transmission Laboratory Quarterly Progress and Status Report, 1960–1999, in-house grey literature, digitized, NOT in PubMed/Scopus) — Fant & Lindqvist diver-speech work and Fant 1972 on wall effects, losses and resonance bandwidths both live here. Undersea Biomedical Research (1974–1993). US Navy Experimental Diving Unit (NEDU) and USAF/Navy technical reports via DTIC. NUTEC (Norwegian Underwater Technology Centre, Bergen) reports. Royal Naval Physiological Laboratory reports. ICASSP 1976–1990. The 1987 European Conference on Speech Technology proceedings on the ISCA Archive (Duncan 1987 on sound-specific shift profiles). Comex Pro internal reports. Patent literature: US 3,950,617 and US 4,342,104 (helium speech unscramblers). Anchor dataset to find first: Belcher & Hatlestad, 'Formant frequencies, bandwidths, and Qs in helium speech', J Acoust Soc Am 74(2):428, 1983 (PMID 6619420) — linear prediction on vowels in air and in heliox at simulated 54–500 msw; reports bandwidths up to 14x air values and Q ratios ~0.3 for low formants to ~2 for high ones.

METHODOLOGICAL TEMPLATE FROM THE RIGHT COMMUNITY. Animal bioacoustics already uses heliox substitution routinely as a source–filter dissociation tool: Europe PMC returns 'The source-filter theory of whistle-like calls in marmosets: Acoustic analysis and simulation of helium-modulated voices' (JASA 2015), 'The acoustic effect of vocal tract adjustments in zebra finches' (2013), 'New perspectives on the physics of birdsong' (2009). Human vocal-tract modellers have an existing human heliox corpus and never use it. Borrow the animal community's protocol.

TRAPS. (1) KILL-CHECK, DO THIS FIRST: a search snippet described a transmission-line vocal-tract model of hyperbaric heliox speech that 'proposes new wall impedance values that match measured closed-tract resonance', attributed to a group at University of Victoria (page https://www.ece.uvic.ca/~bctill/papers/numacoust.html, which returned HTTP 404 when I fetched it; I could NOT resolve this to a published, dated citation). If that work exists as a real publication, THIS TARGET IS DEAD. Resolve it before spending anything else. (2) LPC bandwidth bias: F0 rises with depth (vocal effort), harmonics are sparse relative to upshifted formants, so LPC-estimated bandwidths are inflated. The 14x figure must be bounded or re-derived from raw spectra before it is used as data. (3) Do not reuse the physics-teaching explanation that the sub-proportional formant shift is due to the tract not being fully filled with helium — divers at saturation breathe heliox continuously, so the tract gas IS the breathing gas. That excuse applies to balloon demonstrations, not to the diving corpus, and this is a strength of the target, not a weakness. (4) Articulatory compensation and raised vocal effort at depth are real (Duncan 1987: shift profiles are sound-specific); prefer sustained vowels and closed-tract/closed-glottis conditions, and do not assume a fixed area function across depths without checking.

CANDIDATES I KILLED SO I DID NOT PAD THIS LIST: esophageal/pharyngoesophageal source aerodynamics (modern PES biomechanics and intraluminal-pressure work exists: Takeshita 2013 Head&Neck, Sci Rep 2019, PMC8446905 2021 — premise 'unmeasured' is false); polio-era glossopharyngeal breathing and speech (Dail 1951 is routinely cited; modern receiver too thin); high-level Lombard/shouted speech (Pickett 1956 JASA 28:902 and Pickett & Pollack 1958 JASA 30:669 are cited by modern shouted-speech work — gap is purely bibliographic); nasalance vs velopharyngeal orifice area (Europe PMC co-occurrence = 12 hits incl. 'The relation of nasality and nasalance to nasal port area based on a computational model', Cleft Palate Craniofac J 2012 — already bridged); EPG vs real-time-MRI articulatory timing (14 Europe PMC hits, no clean gap I could establish). || DISCONTINUITY: Commercial and experimental deep manned saturation diving ended, and the research driver for heliox speech intelligibility ended with it. The terminal event: Comex's Hydra 10 simulated dive to 701 msw at the Marseille hyperbaric centre in 1992 — the deepest human dive on record and the last of the Hydra experimental series — after which experimental deep manned diving ceased; Comex divested its diving-services operations in the same period. North Sea deep intervention had already shifted to ROV/diverless systems through the late 1980s, and industry practice settled saturation diving at roughly 120–180 msw, so after 1992 nobody needed to make speech intelligible at 300–700 msw. A second, independently dated and firmer venue discontinuity reinforces it: the primary journal Undersea Biomedical Research ran 1974–1993 and was then renamed/absorbed, and the key Fant & Lindqvist diver-speech measurements were published in KTH's in-house STL-QPSR grey-literature series (1960–1999, ceased), which is not indexed in PubMed or Scopus. CAVEAT I MUST STATE: my WebSearch budget was exhausted before I could re-verify the 1992 Hydra 10 date and the Comex divestiture independently in this session; these come from general knowledge, not from a source I read here. The scout should confirm both as kill-check #0. The STL-QPSR and Undersea Biomedical Research venue facts are the load-bearing, independently checkable half. || PREMISES VERIFIED: CO-OCCURRENCE CHECK ON BARE CONCEPTS, no application words. Europe PMC REST: query ('wall impedance' AND 'vocal tract') AND (helium OR heliox OR hyperbaric) returned hitCount: 1, and the single hit is 'The Respiratory System', Pediatric and Neonatal Mechanical Ventilation, 2013 — i.e. zero on-topic co-occurrence. Control query ('source-filter interaction' OR 'nonlinear source-filter') AND (helium OR heliox OR hyperbaric) returned hitCount: 3, all animal bioacoustics (marmosets JASA 2015; zebra finches 2013; birdsong Phil Trans A 2009), confirming the helium-perturbation method is alive in a different community and absent from human vocal-tract modelling.

REFERENCE LIST I ACTUALLY OPENED AND READ. The most on-point modern document for the receiving side is 'Formant frequencies and bandwidths of the vocal tract transfer function are affected by the mechanical impedance of the vocal tract wall' (Fleischer et al., PMC4490178; PMID 25416844). I fetched the full text. It reports normalised wall impedance inertial component ~250 g/m^2 above ~3 kHz rising to ~2.5x10^5 g/m^2 in the 1.5–3 kHz range, and a dissipative component from 65 to 4.5x10^5 Ns/m^3 — three orders of magnitude, with no confidence intervals, fitted to ONE male subject's inverse-filtered data. Direct quotes I saw: 'Because m/A and b/A are generally unknown, we did an extensive parameter study.' Mean formant and bandwidth deviations fall from 116.5–427.6 Hz with hard walls to 20.2–91.4 Hz with fitted impedance. The paper assumes air throughout, density 1.15 kg/m^3 and sound speed 350 m/s, and does NOT mention helium, heliox, hyperbaric or any gas-mixture perturbation. Its pre-1990 references are Fant 1960; Fant, Nord & Branderud 1976 (wall impedance technical report); Fujimura & Lindqvist 1971 (sweep-tone); Flanagan, Ishizaka & Shipley 1975; Ishizaka, French & Flanagan 1975 (direct determination of wall impedance); Sondhi 1974, 1986; Sondhi & Schroeter 1987; Morse & Ingard 1968; Rothenberg 1973. So it cites the old wall-impedance literature by name but not one item of the hyperbaric corpus.

SECOND RECEIVER, abstract page fetched directly: 'Reconstructing the Vocal Tract with Differentiable Acoustic Simulation', Chen, Lee & Sitzmann, arXiv 2609.36737, submitted 29 Sep 2026, NeurIPS 2026 spotlight. The abstract page does not mention yielding walls, wall impedance or helium. I did NOT read its reference list — the scout must.

ALSO VERIFIED, as counter-evidence I am deliberately conceding: a Birkholz Interspeech 2025 paper states that current simulations treat wall impedance as a damped spring-mass system with constant, potentially speaker-specific values (I could not extract its PDF text, only this statement via search); and modern heliox work exists and DOES cite the old corpus — 'LoRA-enhanced whisper for resource-efficient heliox speech recognition' (PMID 41851160), 'PRL-DAS: Robust Heliox Speech Recognition for Unaligned Low-Resource Data' (MDPI 2026), 'A Helium Speech Correction Method Based on Generative Adversarial Networks' (MDPI 2024), with reference lists containing Lunde, 'Acoustic transmission-line analysis of formants in hyperbaric helium speech', ICASSP 1985, pp. 1141–1144, and Richards & Schafer 1984 on formant bandwidths and frequencies in helium speech. I am NOT claiming these literatures never cite each other. I am claiming the bandwidth/loss-partition use of that corpus is absent, which the hitCount-of-1 check supports.

NOT VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION, flagged honestly: the 1992 Comex Hydra 10 date and the Comex divestiture (WebSearch budget exhausted); the identity of the UVic hyperbaric transmission-line item (URL 404); the reference list of the Chen et al. 2026 paper. || COHERENCE: Yes, and the arithmetic straddles air in the right direction. Ideal-gas numbers relative to air (M=29 g/mol, gamma=1.4, c=350 m/s, rho=1.15 kg/m^3): (a) 98/2 heliox at 51 ATA (500 msw): M=4.56 g/mol, gamma~1.655, c=350*sqrt((1.655/1.4)*(29/4.56))=350*2.74=959 m/s (x2.74); rho=P*M/(RT)=(51*101325*0.00456)/(8.314*310)=9.14 kg/m^3 (x7.95); characteristic impedance rho*c x21.8. (b) 98/2 heliox at 6 ATA (54 msw): c x2.74, rho x0.94 — density essentially air-like while c is nearly tripled. (c) 80/20 heliox at 1 ATA, the cheap modern replication: M=9.6 g/mol, gamma~1.57, c=350*sqrt((1.57/1.4)*(29/9.6))=350*1.84=644 m/s (x1.84); rho=0.38 kg/m^3 (x0.33); rho*c x0.61. So the diving corpus raises rho while the normobaric clinical heliox case LOWERS it, and both raise c. Two regimes on opposite sides of air in density at similar sound speed is precisely the second independent axis needed to separate wall shunt (medium-independent tissue mass and damping), viscous/thermal boundary loss (scales with sqrt(rho*mu*omega)), and radiation loss (scales with rho*c, with (ka)^2 invariant because f scales with c so radiation bandwidth in Hz scales roughly with c). SIGN CHECK, the failure mode I was warned about: yielding walls RAISE F1 above the rigid-tube value and impose a low-frequency floor; at depth the air-column impedance rho*c/A rises ~22x while the tissue impedance is fixed, so the wall's relative shunt effect SHRINKS and measured heliox F1 must fall BELOW a naive proportional scaling of the measured air F1. The classic literature reports exactly this — the measured formant increase is smaller than the full speed-of-sound prediction, nonlinearly and most at low formants. The sign is correct, and the deficit is the wall term. No pressure or temperature regime problem: the replication step runs at 1 atmosphere. || HOW TO CHECK: Three stages, each falsifiable, in increasing cost. STAGE 0 (hours, pure literature): resolve the UVic hyperbaric transmission-line item. If it already fits wall impedance to heliox data, report DEAD and stop. STAGE 1 (days, pure literature): recover the depth-resolved formant frequency AND bandwidth tables from Belcher & Hatlestad 1983 (JASA 74:428), Richards & Schafer ICASSP 1984, Lunde ICASSP 1985, Fant & Lindqvist in STL-QPSR, and any NEDU/NUTEC technical reports, converting cgs acoustic ohms and Q values to Hz and to m/A (g/m^2), b/A (Ns/m^3). Deliverable: one digitised table of bandwidth vs gas density and sound speed. STAGE 2 (weeks, desk simulation, zero subjects): take a published area function and a standard lossy transmission-line or differentiable vocal-tract simulator, and fit (m/A, b/A) jointly to air + the hyperbaric series. The target SUCCEEDS if the three-order-of-magnitude admissible plateau that Fleischer et al. found from air-only data collapses to a narrow basin when the hyperbaric bandwidths are added, and FAILS if it does not — a clean, quantitative, pass/fail outcome computable from published numbers alone. STAGE 3 (optional, cheap, no hyperbaric chamber): record three speakers producing sustained vowels and closed-tract/closed-glottis resonances while breathing normobaric 80/20 heliox (c x1.84, rho x0.33) and confirm the Stage-2 fit predicts the measured formants and bandwidths out of sample on the opposite side of air in density. Standard heliox safety only; 1 atmosphere; no saturation diving required.
targets.domain: Linguistics, phonetics and speech science

targets.problem: Marine CDR by 'organic matter sinking' (baled seaweed, crop residue, wood) needs numbers for three things nobody can yet measure at scale: what fraction of surface-released particulate organic carbon actually reaches >2000 m, how wide the depositional footprint is, and how fast the delivered OC is remineralized or buried once it lands. The United States ran exactly that experiment, under a federal monitoring mandate, between 1986 and 1992: roughly 10^6 tonnes/yr of labile municipal sewage sludge was barged to the surface over the 106-Mile Deepwater Municipal Sludge Site on the Mid-Atlantic continental rise, and EPA/NOAA/USGS tracked its fate to the seafloor with sediment traps and sludge-specific molecular tracers (linear alkylbenzenes, coprostanol/epi-coprostanol). Mine that record for delivered fraction, footprint area, sediment mixing depth and post-cessation decay, and convert it into a bounded source-to-seafloor transfer function for biomass-sinking mCDR.
targets.notes: B-terms (modern vocabulary): organic matter sinking; biomass sinking; sequestration efficiency; transfer efficiency; particle injection; durability; remineralization depth horizon. OLD vocabulary for the same physical quantities: 'waste field', 'sludge plume', 'Deep Water Dumpsite 106' / 'DWD-106' / '106-Mile Site', 'sludge-derived organic matter', 'LABs' (linear alkylbenzenes) and 'coprostanol' as tracers, 'areal extent of sludge-impacted seafloor', 'sediment trap collection efficiency'. DIG IN: NOAA Technical Memorandum NOS ORCA series; the 1990 EPA/NOAA/USCG 'Monitoring, Research, and Surveillance Plan for the 106-Mile Deepwater Municipal Sludge Dump Site and Environs' (Rutgers RUcore record 45238); the 1995 Final Report to Congress; USGS Open-File 94-152; Takada et al. 1994 Environ. Sci. Technol. doi:10.1021/es00055a015; Lamoureux et al. 1996; USGS pub 70016501 'Estimates of the seafloor area impacted by sewage sludge dumped at the 106-Mile site in the Mid-Atlantic Bight' (1991); the earlier NOAA 1974 pre-dumping benthic baseline (repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/66409). Also the NAS/NRC volume at nap.edu/read/312. TRAPS TO AVOID: (1) Do NOT claim the deep sea's response to organic enrichment is unstudied — it is heavily studied via natural falls; the claim is narrower, about this anthropogenic, mass-balanced, monitored release. (2) Do NOT confuse the 106-Mile Site with the shallow 12-Mile New York Bight sludge site (~27 m) — only the deepwater site is in the right depth band. (3) Sludge is MORE labile and finer-grained than baled macroalgae, so delivered-fraction numbers are a LOWER bound on particle delivery and an UPPER bound on remineralization rate; state the bound direction, do not present the numbers as directly transferable. (4) The contaminant load (metals, PCBs, PAHs) is a confound for the ecological response but NOT for the carbon mass balance — keep those two inferences separate. (5) Shelf-ward transport of fines was a live question in the 1990s literature; treat it as the lateral-loss term, not as a flaw. || DISCONTINUITY: The Ocean Dumping Ban Act of 1988 (Pub. L. 100-688) outlawed US municipal sewage sludge disposal at sea; the last barge discharged at the 106-Mile Deepwater Municipal Sludge Site in June 1992, and the federally mandated EPA/NOAA/USCG monitoring programme terminated with its Final Report to Congress in 1995. The London Convention followed with a 1993 amendment banning radioactive and industrial waste dumping (in force 20 February 1994). The research community built around deep-ocean waste disposal was dissolved by statute within three years. || PREMISES VERIFIED: I downloaded and extracted the full text of the single most on-point modern document: Gallo et al. 2025, 'Illuminating deep-sea considerations and experimental approaches for mCDR proposals', Environ. Res. Lett. 20 061003 (11 pp; local copy C:\\Users\\tonyv\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Users-tonyv-Downloads-Haven-Projects-Club-PA\\9a1a4a29-9075-4ef8-ac09-d9d6849af93a\\scratchpad\\gallo.txt). Literal string counts in the extracted text, including its reference list: 'sludge' = 0, 'dump' = 0, 'Dumping' = 0, 'Bight' = 0, 'London Convention' = 0. Its analog sentence, quoted exactly as it appears: "Analogs include storm-driven fluxes of terrestrial matter, such as wood falls, to the deep sea, and the sinking of Sargassum biomass, and vertebrate carcasses." Historical waste disposal appears only as a stressor, quoted exactly: "These activities were assumed harmless due to the large and sparsely inhab-ited nature of the deep sea, and expectations that waste would be permanently removed", and 'waste disposal' is listed among cumulative human pressures. Its reference list includes Bach & Boyd 2021 PNAS 118 e2106147118 on NATURAL analogs, and its only cited organic-addition experiment is "Kelp and wood fall experiments at 1670 m in the Santa Cruz Basin" (Bernardino et al. 2010). Old-corpus side: I confirmed via USGS and NOAA records that the site was used for municipal sludge from 1986 to June 1992; that sludge-derived molecular tracers (LABs, coprostanol, epi-coprostanol) were detected in sediment-trap AND bottom-sediment samples in roughly 2400-2900 m of water ~185 km off New Jersey, penetrating to 6 cm depth by biological and physical mixing; that a 1990 tri-agency monitoring plan specified sediment-trap laboratory parameters; and that a 1991 USGS paper estimated the impacted seafloor area. I did NOT read the 1995 Final Report to Congress itself — the scout must open it. || COHERENCE: Coherent. Release configuration matches the proposal: surface discharge from vessels over 2400-2900 m water, i.e. inside the 1000-4000 m depth band mCDR biomass sinking targets, at ~2-4 degC bottom temperature. No pressure or temperature regime mismatch is involved — the measurement is a mass balance on delivered particulate organic carbon, not a rate law extrapolated across regimes. Arithmetic sanity: ~8 million wet tonnes/yr of sludge at roughly 4% solids and ~30% organic carbon of dry solids gives order 10^5 t C/yr, i.e. comparable to a commercial-scale biomass-sinking deployment, so the signal-to-background ratio against a natural POC rain of order 1-3 g C m^-2 yr^-1 over a footprint of 10^3-10^4 km^2 is detectable rather than marginal — which is consistent with the tracers having in fact been detected in the sediments. The one genuine asymmetry to carry forward, stated with its sign: sludge is finer and more labile than baled macroalgae, so its measured delivered fraction bounds biomass delivery from BELOW and its measured remineralization bounds biomass remineralization from ABOVE. || HOW TO CHECK: High. Concrete extractable numbers: (a) delivered fraction of discharged POC recovered in 1990-91 sediment traps and in surface sediments; (b) impacted seafloor area in km^2 from the 1991 USGS estimate, giving an observed footprint for a known release rate and depth; (c) tracer penetration depth (6 cm) as a bioturbation/burial constraint; (d) post-1992 decay of tracer concentrations in repeat sediment sampling, i.e. an empirical in-situ residence time for delivered labile OC on the abyssal seafloor. Each is a number that either exists in the 1991-1996 documents or does not, so the premise falsifies cleanly in one afternoon of document reading. Failure mode to accept gracefully: if the mass balance was never closed (traps only ever gave presence/absence of tracers), the target degrades to a qualitative analog and should be reported as such rather than inflated.

targets.problem: Does the dissolved-oxygen activity in molten sodium — not the intrinsic chemistry of a coating — control whether sodium wets a substrate, and does its effect invert in sign between substrate classes? The liquid-metal-coolant literature of 1955-1975 measured oxygen in sodium as a SURFACE-ACTIVE SOLUTE with substrate-specific sign, and built instruments to control it (cold traps, plugging meters, electrochemical oxygen meters). The modern solid-state / molten sodium battery literature performs the identical physical operation — wetting molten Na onto NASICON, Na-beta''-alumina, carbon hosts, and oxide 'sodiophilic' coatings at 120-380 C — and treats wettability as an intrinsic property of the coating ('sodiophilicity'), neither controlling nor reporting the oxygen activity of its sodium. If the old result holds, published sodiophilicity rankings are not material properties and are not reproducible between labs using differently-handled sodium.
targets.notes: B-TERMS to bridge on: oxygen activity in liquid sodium; wetting transition temperature; cold trapping; plugging temperature indicator; electrochemical (thoria-yttria) oxygen meter in sodium; sodium chromite (NaCrO2) interfacial layer; Noden oxygen-solubility equation; surface-active solute; Gibbs adsorption of a dissolved gas at a liquid-metal/solid interface. OLD VOCABULARY for the modern quantity: 'sodiophilicity' = the solute-dependence of Na/solid interfacial tension, called 'wetting behaviour vs oxygen content' in 1955-1975. WHERE TO DIG: OSTI.gov full-text for the UKAEA TRG-Report series (TRG-Report-1459 is the anchor; OSTI 4826079), AERE M/R series (AERE M/R 1729 is relevant but is a SCANNED IMAGE pdf with no text layer — it needs OCR, do not waste budget on pdftotext), ANL and HEDL sodium technology reports, the 'Liquid Metals Handbook — Sodium (NaK) Supplement' (1955), Addison's Nottingham group on sodium surface chemistry, and Aust. J. Chem. 1961 for Bradhurst & Buchanan. TRAPS TO AVOID: (1) do NOT state the premise with a single sign — the oxygen effect accelerated wetting on nickel and RETARDED it on stainless steel, and that substrate-dependence IS the finding; a one-signed bridge is the failure mode the brief calls pattern 6. (2) Do NOT propose adding oxygen to sodium: commercial Na is already at or above saturation at these temperatures, so the only coherent manipulation is purification downward. (3) Do NOT drift into room-temperature Na-metal plating/stripping — solid Na at 25 C is a different problem; the target is strictly the MOLTEN wetting step (melt infusion, Na|NASICON and Na|beta''-alumina interface formation, molten-sodium batteries at 110-300 C). (4) The sodium-fast-reactor community is still alive and publishing wetting papers in 2024-25; it is a THIRD literature, not the modern target. Do not claim it does not exist — check instead whether it reports oxygen content, and use it as corroboration of the physics rather than as the gap. (5) Handling note: molten sodium plus oxygen control is genuinely hazardous; this target should be pitched to a group that already handles alkali metals. || DISCONTINUITY: The liquid-metal fast breeder reactor programmes were terminated by a specific sequence of dated political acts, and with them the institutions that published this corpus: (1) the Clinch River Breeder Reactor Project lost its funding in Congress in October 1983 and was terminated; (2) the Fast Flux Test Facility at Hanford was shut down in April 1992; (3) the UKAEA Prototype Fast Reactor at Dounreay shut down 31 March 1994 — UKAEA's Reactor Group at Risley, which issued this corpus as the numbered 'TRG-Report' series, was dissolved and the series ended, with AEA Technology privatised in 1996; (4) the US Integral Fast Reactor programme was cancelled in the FY1995 appropriations and EBR-II shut down 30 September 1994. The sodium surface-chemistry corpus is the orphaned output of those four closures. || PREMISES VERIFIED: VERIFIED BY ME, from primary records I read, not snippets: (1) Todd & Turner, 'Surface Tension of Liquid Sodium and its Wetting Behaviour on Nickel and Stainless Steels', TRG-Report-1459, UKAEA Risley Reactor Group, July 1968 (OSTI 4826079). Verbatim from the abstract: 'Contamination of the sodium with oxygen accelerated the wetting of nickel but retarded that of the stainless steels.' Surface tension measured between 150 and 265 C, comparing sodium at about 5 ppm oxygen against sodium 'close to the solubility limit (10-80 ppm depending on the temperature)'; wetting 'depended strongly on the cleaning process and on the sodium temperature'; method was a vertical-plate zero-buoyancy technique on a small pumped loop that continuously purified the sodium of oxygen under argon. (2) Bradhurst & Buchanan, 'Surface Properties of Liquid Sodium and Sodium-Potassium Alloys in Contact with Metal Oxide Surfaces', Aust. J. Chem. 14(3), 1961, DOI 10.1071/CH9610397 (OSTI 4824222). Verbatim: 'Dissolved oxygen was shown to be surface active in liquid sodium'; wetting of UO2 'was brought about at temperatures above approximately 300 C' when sufficient oxygen was present; 'wetting was more effective on these oxides with larger cations'; Na-K alloys 'showed non-wetting contact angles when relatively free of oxygen' but 'wetting occurred when the oxygen content of the liquid was increased'. (3) CO-OCCURRENCE ON BARE CONCEPTS, Europe PMC, no application words: 'sodiophilic' AND 'wetting' = 36 hits, all 2021-2026 battery papers; 'liquid sodium' AND 'wetting' AND 'fast breeder' = 2 hits, both nuclear instrumentation; intersection empty. 'sodiophilic' AND 'oxygen activity' = 2 hits, both spurious (one is a MOF battery review where 'oxygen activity' means oxygen-reduction activity). (4) REFERENCE LIST ACTUALLY OPENED: 'Interfacial failure mechanisms and design principles in solid-state sodium batteries', Chem. Sci. 2026, PMC12915500 — the most on-point modern review of exactly this interface. 83 references, every one a 2015-2026 materials/electrochemistry journal (Angew 14, Adv Mater 14, Chem Sci 13, ACS AMI 12). Zero references whose titles contain 'oxygen activity', 'dissolved oxygen', 'oxygen content', 'surface tension', 'liquid metal', 'cold trap' or 'fast breeder'. It does cite 'Electro-Chemo-Mechanically Stable and Sodiophilic Interface for Na Metal Anode', confirming the sodiophilicity framing is the field's live vocabulary. NOT VERIFIED, for the scout: whether any individual battery paper reports its sodium's oxygen content; whether the modern Chinese sodium-fast-reactor wetting papers of 2024-25 (which report a 320-335 C wetting transition and a 510-530 C complete-wetting temperature on stainless steel, attributed to Cr2O3) specify oxygen content — if they do not, that is a second instance of the same omission inside the nuclear field itself. || COHERENCE: COHERENT, and the regimes genuinely overlap. Na melts at 97.8 C. Todd & Turner's measurements span 150-265 C; Bradhurst & Buchanan's oxide-wetting onset is ~300 C; battery melt-infusion of Na into hosts and molten-Na wetting of NASICON/beta''-alumina is done at roughly 120-380 C. Fully in regime. ARITHMETIC OF THE CONTROL VARIABLE, which is the one real hazard: oxygen solubility in Na is only single-digit ppm near 150 C rising to tens of ppm by 300 C, while commercial 99.8-99.9% sodium typically carries oxygen at or above that limit. So an unpurified glovebox melt is pinned AT SATURATION, where oxygen activity is unity and NOT a free variable — a naive 'add more oxygen' experiment would be incoherent and must not be proposed. The coherent manipulation is the other direction: go SUB-saturated by cold trapping (a cold finger held at ~120 C fixes oxygen at that temperature's solubility, ~1-5 ppm) or by a Zr/Ti getter foil, exactly as Todd & Turner's pumped purification loop did to reach 5 ppm. This also means the old finding predicts something specific and non-obvious: the apparent sodiophilicity of OXIDE coatings may be an artifact of everyone unknowingly working at oxygen saturation, since Bradhurst & Buchanan observed oxide wetting only when sufficient oxygen was present. Note also that the sign is substrate-specific by construction (accelerates on Ni, retards on stainless steel), so the premise must never be stated as a single-signed 'more oxygen wets better' — that version would fail on the opposite sign for steel. || HOW TO CHECK: Directly testable with equipment a battery lab already has plus a cold finger. Sessile-drop contact angle of molten Na at 150, 200 and 250 C on (i) bare NASICON Na3Zr2Si2PO12, (ii) Na-beta''-alumina, (iii) two or three of the literature's standard 'sodiophilic' coatings including at least one oxide (ZnO, SnO2 or Al2O3) and one carbon, each measured at two controlled oxygen activities: saturated (as-received Na, no trap) versus cold-trapped at ~120 C to ~1-5 ppm, with the oxygen level set by trap temperature and, if available, read by a plugging-temperature indicator or a thoria-yttria electrochemical oxygen meter — both LMFBR-era instruments whose designs are in the same orphaned report series. PREDICTION THAT DISCRIMINATES: the ranking of substrates by contact angle changes between the two oxygen levels, and for at least one substrate class the sign of the oxygen effect is opposite to another, per Todd & Turner. A null result (ranking invariant over 1-30 ppm O) kills the target cleanly. Secondary, zero-cost check: survey the 36 'sodiophilic' papers and count how many state the oxygen content or supplier grade of their sodium — a near-zero count establishes the confound even before any new measurement.

targets.problem: The silver-halide photographic industry solved, quantified and ran at industrial scale the problem of precipitating monodisperse ionic-halide crystals of selected crystal habit, reproducibly, by holding the FREE SILVER/HALIDE ION ACTIVITY constant in a closed potentiometric feedback loop during double-jet precipitation (constant pAg), with habit-controlling agents that switch the expressed face between {100}, {110} and {111}. The metal-halide perovskite nanocrystal field faces the same physical problem — monodispersity, habit control, and an acknowledged batch-to-batch reproducibility problem in an ionic halide crystal whose halide exchanges freely with the medium — and has never imported that control strategy, closing its loops instead on the product's optical output. The question: does constant-halide-activity feedback precipitation transfer to CsPbX3 and related halides, and does it fix the reproducibility problem?
targets.notes: B-TERMS to bridge on: pAg; pBr; controlled double-jet and triple-jet precipitation; constant-pAg; habit modifier / habit-controlling agent; silver-ion-selective electrode in feedback; physical ripening and ripening agents (thioether, thiocyanate, ammonia) as solubility-complexing accelerants of Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner narrowing; nucleation-then-growth separation at constant supersaturation. OLD VOCABULARY for modern quantities: 'pAg/pBr' = free halide activity / supersaturation driving force; 'habit modifier' = facet-selective additive; 'ripening agent' = deliberate solubility enhancer used to NARROW rather than broaden the distribution, which is the inverted intuition most worth stealing. WHERE TO DIG: Google Patents is the primary archive, not the journals — search assignees Eastman Kodak, Fuji Photo Film, Agfa-Gevaert with 'controlled double jet' and 'pAg'; then the Society of Photographic Scientists and Engineers journals (Photographic Science and Engineering, Journal of Imaging Science) via HathiTrust and Internet Archive, which hold the pre-1990 volumes that are not in Scopus; also Berichte der Bunsengesellschaft and the Journal of Photographic Science for the physical-chemistry fraction. TRAPS TO AVOID: (1) do NOT claim the field is unaware that halide activity matters — the 2021 review says so explicitly; the claim is narrowly about the absent closed-loop potentiometric control and the quantified constant-activity protocol. Overstating this is failure pattern 4. (2) Do NOT propose ISE feedback in hot-injection/octadecene chemistry; restrict to DMF/DMSO/GBL antisolvent routes. (3) Do NOT map AgBr facets onto perovskite facets; the bridge is activity thermodynamics only. (4) Verify the autonomous-synthesis control variables BEFORE anything else — that is the single most likely killer. (5) This target is lower confidence than the sodium one; if budget is tight, fund the sodium target first. || DISCONTINUITY: The industry that owned this corpus was displaced outright by digital imaging, on dated record: AgfaPhoto GmbH filed for insolvency on 27 May 2005, and Eastman Kodak filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 19 January 2012, dismantling Kodak Research Laboratories, which was the principal publisher of silver-halide precipitation physical chemistry. The knowledge was carried overwhelmingly by corporate research labs (Kodak, Fuji, Agfa) and by their patent estate rather than by a university community, so when the labs were liquidated there was no academic successor to carry the corpus forward — the same structural pattern as the fluidics industry killed by cheap silicon. || PREMISES VERIFIED: VERIFIED BY ME, by opening the reference list, not from snippets: the single most on-point modern document is Dey et al., 'State of the Art and Prospects for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals', ACS Nano 2021 (PMC8482768) — a consensus multi-author review with 817 references. I retrieved and searched all 817: ZERO contain 'silver halide', 'photographic', 'pAg', 'double jet', 'habit modifier', 'gelatin', 'Kodak', or 'ripening agent'. The only 'emulsion' hit is 'Emulsion Synthesis of Size-Tunable CH3NH3PbBr3 Quantum Dots', an unrelated droplet route; the only 'sensitiz' hits are photovoltaic/upconversion sensitisation. I also read the review's own text: it does recognise the concept, stating 'the Br- equilibrium between the nanocube and the reaction medium' and that 'the acidity of the reaction environment controlled the reactivity of the PbX2 precursor', and it flags purification sensitivity ('Overwashing can lead to irreversible aggregation, changes in morphology, a significant drop in photoluminescence'). So the CONCEPT that halide activity matters is NOT novel to the field — the claim is strictly about the absent measurement-and-control instrument and the quantified constant-activity protocol. Be precise about this or the target collapses into pattern 4. OLD-SIDE CONTENT VERIFIED from US patent full texts: constant-pAg controlled double-jet is described as the standard method ('a controlled double-jet method wherein a silver halide is formed with the pAg of a liquid phase medium held constant', yielding 'grains having a regular crystallographic shape and a uniform grain size'); habit is switchable ('(111) faces start to appear in a cube to form a tetradecahedron ... This tetradecahedron changes into an octahedron in which all faces are (111)'); and a 1978 triple-jet AgCl process with Cd2+ at controlled pAg and pH gave 'rhombododecahedral {110}, octahedral {111}, and cubic {100} crystal habits'. CO-OCCURRENCE ON BARE CONCEPTS, Europe PMC: 'silver halide emulsion' AND 'perovskite' = 1 hit, a 2017 historical essay on photography-to-solar charge transfer; 'photographic emulsion' AND 'perovskite nanocrystal' = 0; 'potentiometric' AND 'nanocrystal synthesis' AND 'ion selective' = 0. NOT VERIFIED, for the scout, because this session's web-search budget was exhausted: (i) the exact journal-succession dates for Photographic Science and Engineering / Journal of Imaging Science and the SPSE-to-IS&T rename — I assert the industrial collapse dates above, which I am confident of, but the scout should confirm the journal chronology before using it; (ii) my claim that the autonomous/self-driving perovskite-nanocrystal platforms close their loops on photoluminescence spectra rather than on ion activity — Europe PMC shows 8 such autonomous-microfluidics papers exist (e.g. 'Autonomous microfluidic experimentation for exploring reaction inference and synthesizing double perovskite nanoplatelets', 2026) but I did not read their control variables. CONFIRM THIS FIRST: if any of them already uses an ion-activity sensor in feedback, the target is dead. || COHERENCE: COHERENT ONLY IN A POLAR MEDIUM, and this must be specified or the experiment is physically incoherent. A halide-activity electrode (a Ag/AgBr or Ag/AgI wire, or a halide ISE) requires an ion-conducting solvent and a stable reference junction. It therefore works for the LARP / antisolvent-crystallisation route run from DMF, DMSO or gamma-butyrolactone at roughly 20-60 C, and for aqueous or alcoholic analogue systems. It does NOT work for hot-injection synthesis in octadecene with oleylamine and oleic acid at 140-200 C: that medium is effectively non-conducting, has no usable reference junction, and would chemically attack a Ag/AgX couple. Prescribing constant-pX feedback for hot injection would be exactly the wrong-regime error. Second coherence point: the analogy is at the level of ION-ACTIVITY THERMODYNAMICS (supersaturation and surface ion excess set by free halide activity), not crystallographic facet analogy — AgBr is rock-salt and CsPbBr3 is perovskite, so their {hkl} faces are NOT counterparts, and any claim that transfers a specific AgBr facet result to a specific perovskite facet is unfounded. Keep the bridge thermodynamic. Third: the arithmetic is favourable in principle — pX control to +/-0.05 corresponds to about +/-12% in free halide activity at 25 C (59 mV per decade), i.e. feedback tightens the driving force far beyond what nominal stoichiometric mixing achieves, which is the quantitative reason the method produced monodisperse grains industrially. || HOW TO CHECK: Testable on a benchtop with a jacketed reactor, two syringe pumps and a potentiostat/pH-meter input. Run the standard DMF-or-DMSO antisolvent (LARP) synthesis of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals two ways at 20-60 C: (a) conventional fixed-rate reagent addition, and (b) double-jet addition of the Pb/Cs stream and the Br stream under closed-loop control of a Ag/AgBr (or Br-ISE) electrode holding pBr constant to +/-0.05, with the setpoint scanned across several values in separate runs. PREDICTIONS THAT DISCRIMINATE: (i) the pBr setpoint, not nominal stoichiometry, selects mean size and the cube-versus-platelet habit, monotonically; (ii) run-to-run dispersion of size and of PL linewidth across 5-10 repeats falls substantially under feedback relative to fixed-rate addition. A null result — setpoint has no systematic effect, or dispersion does not improve — kills it. Two cheap pre-experiment literature checks that can kill it faster and should be done first: read the control variables of the 8 autonomous-microfluidic perovskite papers, and patent-search for any halide-ISE feedback in perovskite or metal-halide crystallisation.
